result.topic_en: Calculation of log k (the modulus of elliptic functions, via its q-series with q = e^{xi}) at rational boundary points x = 2mπ/n, mπ/n and mπ/(2n), reducing the limits to finite sums involving roots of unity and the integer-part function E.
result.transcription:
Riemann 14

$\underline{II}$

$\log k = \log 4\sqrt{q} + \sum (-1)^n \frac{4}{n} \frac{q^n}{1+q^n}$ , $q = e^{xi}$

1) $x = \frac{2m}{n}\pi$, $n$ ungerade[?]

$\log k = i\left(\frac{x}{2} + \sum (-1)^s \frac{2}{s} \operatorname{tg} s\frac{x}{2}\right)$

$= i\left(\frac{x}{2} + \sum_{0,\infty}^{t} \sum_{1,2n}^{s} (-1)^s \frac{2}{2nt+s} \operatorname{tg}\frac{sm}{n}\pi\right)$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + 2i\int_0^1 \sum_{1,2n}^{s} (-1)^s \operatorname{tg}\frac{sm}{n}\pi \frac{x^{s-1}dx}{1-x^{2n}}$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + 2\int_0^1 \sum_{1,2n}^{s} (-1)^s \frac{\alpha^{2sm}-1}{\alpha^{2sm}+1} \frac{1}{2n} \sum_{1,2n}^{t} \frac{\alpha^{-ts}\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x}$ , $\alpha = e^{\frac{2\pi i}{2n}}$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + \frac{1}{2n}\int_0^1 \sum_{1,2n}^{t} \frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x}\, 2\sum_{1,n-1}^{\sigma}\sum_{1,2n}^{s} (-1)^{s+\sigma-1} \alpha^{s(2m\sigma - t)}$

$\frac{1}{1+r\alpha^{2sm}} = \sum_{0,2n-1}^{\sigma} \frac{(-1)^\sigma \alpha^{2s\sigma m} r^\sigma}{1-r^{2n}} = -\frac{1}{2n}\sum_{0,2n-1}^{\sigma} (-1)^\sigma \sigma \alpha^{2s\sigma m}$

$= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{0,n-1}^{\sigma} (-1)^\sigma \alpha^{2s\sigma m}$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + 2\sum_{1,n-1}^{\sigma} \log(1-\alpha^{n+2m\sigma})(-1)^\sigma$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + \sum_{1,n-1}^{\sigma} \log \alpha^{2m\sigma} (-1)^\sigma$

$= i\frac{x}{2} + 2\pi i\left(\sum_{1,n-1}^{\sigma} \frac{2m\sigma}{2n}(-1)^\sigma - \sum_{1,n-1}^{\sigma} (-1)^\sigma E\left(\frac{2m\sigma}{2n}+\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)$

2) $x = \frac{m}{n}\pi$, $m, n$ ungerade.

$\log k = -\frac{q+q_0}{q-q_0}\frac{3}{2n^2}\sum_{1,\infty}\frac{1}{s^2} - \frac{1}{n}\log\frac{1+q^n}{1-q^n} + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\int_0^1 \sum_{1,4n-1}^{s} (-1)^s \frac{x^{s-1}dx}{1-x^{4n}} \frac{\alpha^{2ms}-1}{\alpha^{2ms}+1}$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\int_0^1 \sum_{1,4n}^{t} \frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x} \frac{1}{4n}\cdot\frac{-1}{2n} \sum_{1,4n-1}^{s}\sum_{0,2n-1}^{\sigma} (-1)^{s+\sigma} \sigma \alpha^{2s\sigma m}(\alpha^{2ms}-1)\alpha^{-st}$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\cdot 2\pi i \sum_{1,n-1}^{s} \frac{s}{n}(-1)^s\left(\frac{ms-n}{2n} - E\frac{ms}{n}\right)$ , $m\mu \equiv 1 \mod. 2n$

$= A + \pi i\left(\frac{m-\mu}{2} + \frac{\mu}{2n} + 2\sum_{1,n-1}^{s} E\frac{\mu s}{2n}(-1)^s - 2\sum_{1,n-1}^{s} E\frac{ms}{2n}(-1)^s\right)$

3) $x = \frac{m}{2n}\pi$, $m$ ungerade.

$\log k = \frac{q+q_0}{q-q_0}\frac{3}{8n^2}\sum\frac{1}{s^2} + \frac{1}{2n}\log\frac{1+q^{2n}}{1-q^{2n}}$

$+ \frac{x}{2}i + \sum^{t}\sum_{1,8n-1}^{s} (-1)^s \frac{2}{8nt+s} \operatorname{tg} s\frac{m}{4n}\pi$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\int_0^1 \sum_{1,8n-1}^{s} \frac{x^{s-1}dx}{1-x^{8n}} \frac{\alpha^{2ms}-1}{\alpha^{2ms}+1}(-1)^s$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\int_0^1 \sum_{1,8n}^{t} \frac{\alpha^t dx}{1-\alpha^t x} \frac{1}{8n}\cdot\frac{-1}{4n}\sum_{1,8n-1}^{s}\sum_{0,4n-1}^{\sigma} (-1)^{s+\sigma}\sigma\alpha^{2s\sigma m}(\alpha^{2ms}-1)\alpha^{-st}$

$t = 2rm + 4n \mod. 8n$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\sum_{1,4n-1}^{r} \log(1-\alpha^{4n+2rm}) \frac{1}{8n}\cdot\frac{1}{4n}\left(8n((-1)^{r-1}(r-1) - (-1)^r r) + 8n(-1)^r(4n-1)\right)$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i + 2\sum_{-2n+1,\,2n-1}^{s} \log(1-\alpha^{2sm})\frac{-s}{2n}(-1)^s$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i - 4\sum_{0,2n-1}^{s} \log(-\alpha)^{2sm}\frac{s}{4n}(-1)^s$

$= A + \frac{x}{2}i - 4\sum_{0,2n-1}^{s}\left(\frac{sm}{4n}\right)\frac{s}{4n}(-1)^s 2\pi i$ $\quad (x) =$ absolut kleinster Rest von $x$

methods.what: q-series expansion of log k (elliptic modulus) with q = e^{xi}
Writing the series at rational x as an integral over [0,1] of a rational function and decomposing via 2n-th roots of unity
Partial-fraction expansion of 1/(1+r α^{2sm}) over powers of the root of unity
Value of log k at x = 2mπ/n as finite sum with integer-part function E
Asymptotic of log k near x = mπ/n (m,n odd) as A plus finite Dedekind-type sum with mμ ≡ 1 mod 2n
Asymptotic of log k near x = mπ/(2n) (m odd) as finite sum using absolutely least residue (x)
